chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: A show-business band after Eckstine: shuffle rhythm and chartreuse uniforms
summary: Jordan's music was mostly vocals and shows, a contrast to the Eckstine band, but he finds it enjoyable with good musicians.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Altogether, it was a very nice and different kind of experience, because being in a band like that was quite different than anything that I had been in. First of all, the kind of stuff that Louis Jordan was doing, after coming out of a band like the Eckstine band, with Charlie Parker and people like that. You know, we were sitting up playing this shuffle rhythm, and these almost... What we played were usually...80 percent vocals that Louis sang during the night. Of course, the musicians had solos, but the overall thing was a more show business type thing than it was actually a musical thing.
Plus the fact that of our uniforms... I remember one was green. We had a chartreuse uniform. And we had another, red or something... But wearing these kind of uniforms was

something where the guys in the Eckstine band would have laughed anybody off the stand if they saw this kind of thing. But a lot of times, you see situations that you say you might not be caught dead in... You have to be careful about what you say, because you might just wind up being in a situation like that, under certain circumstances.

Nevertheless, it really showed me that if you're a musician, sometimes you've got to play all sorts and types of jobs, and if you're playing with guys who are good musicians and good personalities, it can be an enjoyable situation.
